title: Superpowers Race to Put Nuclear Reactors on the Moon
summary: The United States wants a reactor on the moon by 2030. A Russian-Chinese alliance is working on one for 2036. Some leading scientists say the danger is great.

title: Who Owns the Moon?
summary: A treaty from the 1960s declared that nobody can own outer space. Half a century later, billionaires and superpowers see fortunes to be made nonetheless.

title: Houthis Claim Attack on Aramco as Yemen Conflict Escalates
summary: The announcement follows weeks of fighting with the Iran-allied armed group and threatens to deepen U.S. involvement in the widening Middle East conflict.

title: Iran’s Top Security Official Warns of Dire Economic Crisis
summary: The rare admission from Mohsen Rezaei, the security chief, came weeks after the U.S. tightened sanctions and its naval blockade.

title: How Cornell Punished Each of the 7 Men Accused of Sexual Assault
summary: Summaries obtained by The New York Times offer a detailed look at the discipline meted out to the men accused of sexually assaulting a fellow student at Cornell University.

title: After Week of Turmoil at Cornell, a Heavy Cloud Hangs Over Student Life
summary: As the weekend arrived, much of the nightlife in the upstate New York college town was subdued. But there were still some students looking to cut loose.

title: Cornell Case Carries Far-Reaching Implications for Hochul and James
summary: The decision to intercede by Gov. Kathy Hochul and the New York attorney general, Letitia James, has raised questions of impartiality as both face re-election.

title: How Trump Moved Ethical Lines With His Ads, Businesses and Summits
summary: The president’s decision to hold an international summit at his own private golf club, an idea rejected in his first term, illustrates how much he has shattered norms.

title: Kristi Noem’s Agency Gave Her Donor a Lucrative Contract Just Before She Left
summary: The Homeland Security Department signed a multi-million dollar agreement to buy five aircraft from a company owned by a political contributor of the secretary on her last day, documents show.

title: Democrats Lead Governor Races Deep in Republican Territory, Polls Show
summary: Democratic advantages in the races for governor in Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska reflect deep unhappiness with President Trump and the economy. A Republican leads in Kansas.

title: Some Democrats Say Senate Race In South Carolina Is Winnable. Others, not so much.
summary: Dr. Annie Andrews, a Democrat, is hoping to defeat Senator Darline Graham. Even some of her most ardent supporters sense that her bid is a long shot.

title: How Kansas Suddenly Became a Battleground State for Senate Control
summary: The state hasn’t elected a Democrat to the Senate in nearly a century. Economic challenges during President Trump’s second term, as well as other factors, have put it in play.

title: ‘No Tax on Tips’ May Fall Flat for G.O.P. in Fight for House and Senate
summary: Tipped workers in Arizona have benefited from the G.O.P.’s big tax cut. But they face economic stress from other Republican policies.

title: Dying Patients Are Inundated by Misinformation. My Dad Was One of Them.
summary: Cancer patients are being persuaded to spend tens of thousands on unproven treatments by alternative-medicine clinics.

title: The ‘God Gap’ Is Narrowing in Texas
summary: It may not be enough for James Talarico to win. But might it also be a sign of a change to come?

title: The Met Gala Needs a Razzle-Dazzle Reset: Bob Mackie
summary: “Bob did costumes, and fashion people looked down on him for some reason.”

title: Biljana Plavsic, a Former Bosnian Serb Political Leader, Has Died
summary: Biljana Plavsic, a Bosnian Serb, pleaded guilty to one count of crimes against humanity. She later recanted and said she “would do the same again.”
